project-recovery.html.title: Recovery Readiness Auditor
project-recovery.html.evidence: Public source, preserved archive, sample data, CLI behavior, and automated tests
project-recovery.html.problem: Backup configuration is not evidence of recoverability. The project turns recovery objectives, ownership, backup age, restore-test cadence, and runbook references into explicit findings that can be reviewed before an incident.
constraints: Offline operation against declared inventory
No credentials, network discovery, or production mutation
Time-bound checks must behave correctly across malformed input, missing fields, duplicates, and timezone boundaries
architecture: Input validation and normalized service records
Policy checks for RPO/RTO evidence, ownership, backup freshness, restore-test age, and runbook presence
Human-readable and machine-readable output paths designed for repeatable review
verification: Automated tests cover boundary conditions, malformed data, duplicate services, timezone offsets, and CLI behavior
Fictional sample services produce known expected findings
Preserved archive and public source allow independent inspection
reproduce: Run the project against the included fictional inventory
Execute the automated test suite
Change backup age, ownership, or restore-test dates and verify the resulting finding changes deterministically
project-recovery.html.limitations: This audits declared recovery evidence; it does not execute a restore, prove data integrity, or establish business acceptance of a recovered service.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Recovery evidence is sufficient only when policy checks and a successful restoration can be demonstrated separately.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic service inventory with one outdated backup, one missing runbook and one stale restore test; vary time zones and RPO/RTO thresholds.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Expected policy findings match an independently calculated table; malformed and duplicate records cause an explicit result, not silent acceptance.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A clean policy report despite an expired restore test or negative RPO proves the checker missed a boundary.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Versioned fictional inventory, expected/actual findings, exact CLI invocation, test results and a statement that no production restore occurred.

project-dependency.html.title: Infrastructure Dependency Analyzer
project-dependency.html.evidence: Public source, declared topology fixtures, graph analysis, and documented evidence boundary
project-dependency.html.problem: Flat inventories hide dependency chains. The project models directed service dependencies so change impact, circular prerequisites, recovery ordering, and downstream risk can be examined explicitly.
constraints: Declared dependencies are hypotheses until validated against the real environment
Cycles and directional edges must remain visible rather than silently flattened
Analysis must remain offline and explainable
architecture: Directed graph of services and dependencies
Path traversal for upstream/downstream impact and recovery sequencing
Cycle detection and recovery-target alignment checks
verification: Known graph fixtures expose expected paths and circular dependencies
Individual paths can be traced edge by edge
Source is available for independent algorithm review
reproduce: Load a small declared service graph
Introduce a dependency edge or cycle
Compare the resulting impact paths and recovery order to the expected graph reasoning
project-dependency.html.limitations: A graph can only be as accurate as its declared edges; real production dependencies require observation and owner validation.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: The change-impact graph identifies downstream consumers without inventing undeclared production dependencies.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Five-node directed topology with redundant upstream connections, a missing dependency and a deliberate cycle.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Compare reachability and downstream blast radius before and after removing one link, preserving directed-edge semantics.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: An unrelated node appears affected, a reachable service is omitted, or a cycle causes nontermination.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Input graph, edge assumptions, expected dependency sets, graph output and a list of unobserved real dependencies.

project-lifecycle.html.title: Employee Lifecycle Toolkit
project-lifecycle.html.evidence: Public source, deterministic planning model, projected state, and audit-oriented output
project-lifecycle.html.problem: Joiner, mover, and leaver operations cross identity, authorization, ownership, and compliance boundaries. The project separates requested change, policy decision, planned action, projected state, and audit evidence.
constraints: Safe planning before mutation
Idempotent behavior when workflows resume or retry
Approval and policy boundaries must remain explicit
architecture: Declared directory snapshot plus employee request and access policy
Policy-gated action planner with projected post-change state
Audit record that distinguishes requested, approved, planned, and denied actions
verification: Deterministic fixtures make repeat runs comparable
Dry-run planning avoids claiming live directory mutation
Source can be inspected for policy and idempotency behavior
reproduce: Load a bounded fictional identity snapshot
Run onboarding, role-change, and offboarding cases
Repeat a request and verify the plan does not accumulate duplicate effects
project-lifecycle.html.limitations: This portfolio evidence does not establish live execution against an enterprise identity platform or validate a customer tenant.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A lifecycle request can be planned deterministically without accidentally granting permissions or changing real identities.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic joiner/mover/leaver identities with duplicate requests, conflicting roles and a failed approval.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Verify least-privilege target state, no live mutations in dry-run, and idempotent rerun outcomes.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: Duplicate requests create additional access, or a rejected approval still emits a grant action.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Fictional request, identity mapping, approval matrix, pre/post plan diff and audit log.

project-fusion.html.title: Providing Energy from Fusion
project-fusion.html.posture: Engineering coursework and technical communication artifact
project-fusion.html.evidence: Coursework framing, systems-level analysis, preserved project narrative, and explicit scientific/economic claim boundaries
project-fusion.html.problem: Fusion-energy discussions often collapse plasma physics, engineering gain, plant economics, risk, and public policy into one claim. The project separates those layers and communicates the tradeoffs to a non-specialist audience.
constraints: Team communication artifact rather than an experimental physics result
Scientific claims must remain distinct from economic or policy claims
Presentation clarity must not erase uncertainty
architecture: Systems-level framing from plasma conditions to whole-plant considerations
Separation of technical feasibility, engineering risk, economics, and stakeholder impact
Narrative and visual structure designed for public technical communication
verification: The project page preserves the authored engineering question, approach, and systems framing
Claims are bounded as technical communication and research synthesis rather than experimental validation
The missing original recording is disclosed rather than represented by a broken or unverifiable media link
reproduce: Review the project framing and separate plasma-physics, engineering-gain, plant-economics, and policy claims
Select one technical claim and independently trace it to current authoritative evidence
Extend the project by adding a preserved presentation artifact or transcript only when its provenance and bytes are available
project-fusion.html.limitations: This project does not reproduce a fusion experiment, measure plasma performance, or establish commercial feasibility.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A positive plasma energy-gain factor does not by itself establish positive net electric output.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Illustrative heating power, fusion power, plant efficiency and balance-of-plant consumption; use published values only when dated and attributed.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Calculate Q_plasma and plant net power separately with units; perturb auxiliary power and conversion efficiency.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A positive Q_plasma is presented as measured plant profitability or total electricity gain without inputs.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Equations, assumptions, sensitivity table, cited fusion source and explicit non-claims.

project-portfolio.html.title: Engineering Portfolio
project-portfolio.html.evidence: Public deployment, GitHub source, responsive UI, accessibility controls, deployment/rollback workflow, and ongoing release history
project-portfolio.html.problem: A technical portfolio must remain fast, accessible, maintainable, and trustworthy while combining professional history, interactive labs, games, research content, and a large learning system on static university hosting.
constraints: Static OSU hosting with no application backend
Progressive enhancement and usable navigation if optional features fail
Responsive behavior across desktop, mobile, and specialized interactive pages
architecture: Semantic HTML, shared design tokens, CSS layout system, and plain JavaScript
Global navigation/theme/audio/resilience layers shared across heterogeneous pages
Isolated deployment namespaces, backups, public verification, and rollback-aware update scripts
verification: The site itself is the live artifact
Source history records iterative changes and preservation constraints
Deployment scripts perform public verification after updates
reproduce: Clone the repository and serve it as a static site
Inspect shared CSS/JavaScript ownership and page-specific overrides
Run the repository project-quality checks and compare local behavior with the public site
project-portfolio.html.limitations: The site intentionally avoids a backend, authentication service, and framework runtime; some specialized labs are educational simulations rather than production systems.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A release should be reproducible from an immutable source revision without altering protected creative files.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Staged change to a harmless content fixture with fixed Git SHA; inject a failing public check and cache delay.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Verify source/deployed hashes, rollback to previous entry page, protected-file hash stability and public response provenance.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A successful exit occurs when the expected module is missing, the wrong revision is served or a protected hash changes.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Source commit, release manifest, server and public checks, backup location and recovery test results.

project-qubit.html.title: One qubit. Two outcomes.
project-qubit.html.evidence: Interactive browser model, source repository, analytic test cases, executable notebooks, and explicitly bounded claims
project-qubit.html.problem: Computational-basis probabilities alone hide phase. The project makes a general single-qubit state inspectable across X, Y, and Z measurement bases while separating ideal mathematics from hardware claims.
constraints: Single-qubit classical simulation only
No entanglement or quantum-hardware claim
Probability calculations must remain consistent with normalized state amplitudes and basis changes
architecture: Bloch-sphere state parameterization using θ and φ
Companion density-operator treatment for amplitude damping and mixed-state reasoning
verification: Known analytic states provide exact expected probabilities
Executable notebooks independently calculate reference cases
Source and interactive implementation can be compared directly
reproduce: Set θ and φ to known pole/equator states
Compare X/Y/Z probabilities against analytic expectations
Use the damping companion to compare pure-state and mixed-state behavior
project-qubit.html.limitations: This is a classical simulation of quantum state mathematics; it is not a quantum processor or a two-qubit entanglement experiment.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A classical single-qubit model reproduces Born-rule probabilities without implying quantum hardware execution.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Normalized amplitudes for |0⟩, |+⟩ and phase-shifted states; vary measurement basis and seed.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Check Σp=1 and compare Z/X/Y probabilities against an independent analytic calculation.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: Global phase changes predicted probabilities, a negative probability appears or finite shots are reported as exact outcomes.
reviewProtocol.evidence: State vector, analytic table, simulator output, seed and numerical tolerance.

project-learning-library.html.title: Cloud & Systems Knowledge Library
project-learning-library.html.evidence: Published lessons, guided paths, interactive labs, stable content identifiers, and reproducible foundation experiments
project-learning-library.html.problem: Technical learning systems often optimize for content volume rather than verified understanding. This project connects concepts, experiments, evidence, review, and active recall across infrastructure domains.
constraints: Generated breadth must not be mislabeled as individually reviewed depth
Stable lesson/path identifiers must survive content upgrades
Claims should be source-linked and experiments bounded by what they actually demonstrate
architecture: Interactive experiments, guided paths, glossary, practice, and evidence review surfaces
Progress and navigation systems layered over static content
verification: Published authored lessons and runnable foundation experiments are separated from broader catalog metadata
Stable IDs preserve compatibility across upgrades
Source-linked learning objects expose evidence and limitations
reproduce: Choose a lesson and follow its source/evidence path
Run the associated lab or notebook
Use the active-recall/review surfaces and compare the result with the source material
project-learning-library.html.limitations: Catalog size is not a claim that every topic has equal editorial depth or that completing the platform constitutes formal certification.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A large lesson catalog is useful only when prerequisites, references, practice and measurable progress remain traceable.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Select seven foundation lessons, one deliberate broken reference and an assessment with shuffled options.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Verify stable lesson IDs, resolved dependencies, correct answer mapping and browser-local progress restoration.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A broken link is marked verified, a retry changes the answer mapping or mere page opening implies mastery.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Lesson IDs, source citations, assessment rubric, screenshot or test log, and editorial-review boundary.

project-advanced-computing.html.title: Advanced Computing Learning Library
project-advanced-computing.html.evidence: Authored advanced-computing sequence, executable CPU companions, analytic references, and bounded scientific claims
project-advanced-computing.html.problem: Advanced computing concepts become misleading when visualizations are detached from mathematics, assumptions, or reproducible calculations. The project connects architecture, linear algebra, HPC, AI, and quantum foundations to explicit checks.
constraints: Educational models must state assumptions
CPU teaching experiments cannot imply accelerator or quantum advantage
Numerical output should be compared against analytic or independently computed references when possible
architecture: Connected learning paths across architecture, memory, parallelism, HPC, GPUs, math, physics, and quantum topics
Executable teaching companions for selected calculations
Evidence/review surfaces that distinguish model, calculation, and claim
verification: Selected calculations have executable CPU references
Exact or analytic comparisons are used where appropriate
Scope statements prevent educational simulations from being presented as hardware benchmarks
reproduce: Select a calculation and derive its expected result independently
Run the companion implementation
Compare assumptions, numerical output, and the evidence required to extend the claim
project-advanced-computing.html.limitations: This is an advanced learning/research platform, not evidence of hardware speedup, production HPC deployment, or graduate credentialing.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Performance claims must distinguish ideal models from actual throughput, latency and hardware measurements.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic strong- and weak-scaling workloads with serial fraction, data-transfer overhead and one GPU allocation constraint.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Compute Amdahl-bound speedup and compare modeled compute/communication tradeoffs across processor counts.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A modeled speedup exceeds its stated bound without an accounted assumption, or is labeled real hardware evidence.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Workload definition, scaling equations, baseline, sensitivity curve and provenance for any measured data.

play-evil-wizard.html.title: Defeat the Evil Wizard
play-evil-wizard.html.posture: Playable browser game and protected runtime export
play-evil-wizard.html.evidence: Dedicated launcher, hosted playable build, device-adaptive controls, and preserved runtime boundary
play-evil-wizard.html.problem: A browser game has to support actual play—not just screenshots—while adapting controls and launch behavior across desktop, tablet, phone, and handheld contexts.
constraints: Protected game export must remain a complete versioned unit
Input/control mode must adapt to device capability
Launcher and showcase code must not silently modify the runtime assets
architecture: Portfolio showcase separated from dedicated game launcher/runtime
Protected hosted export kept isolated from unrelated website content changes
verification: The live hosted game is the primary functional artifact
Launch/relaunch and device-mode checks are separate from portfolio-page tests
Runtime/PCK/WASM assets are treated as an atomic release surface
reproduce: Open the dedicated game launcher
Select a champion and control mode
Launch, restart, and return to the menu on a supported browser/device
play-evil-wizard.html.limitations: The portfolio page does not claim that unrelated notebook or website tests validate the game runtime; full acceptance requires the hosted-game gate.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: The released browser game can launch and recover using its protected deployed runtime.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Open the current hosted game in desktop/phone test environments; record start, return, restart and load outcomes without modifying assets.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Verify launch-to-play, controls, restart and preserved asset hashes independently from generic portfolio checks.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A broken launch or missing export is incorrectly treated as passing because its surrounding portfolio page loads.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Host-only export checklist, device/browser record, timestamps, screenshots and unchanged build checksum.

project-asset-inventory.html.title: Asset Inventory Reconciler
project-asset-inventory.html.evidence: Public source, exported sample data, offline reports, schema handling, and reproducible reconciliation behavior
project-asset-inventory.html.problem: Asset inventories drift when exports contain duplicate, missing, malformed, or contradictory records. The project compares snapshots and makes mismatches visible in human- and machine-readable forms.
constraints: Offline operation against exported data
No endpoint discovery or production inventory mutation
Matching keys and conflict ownership must be explicit
architecture: Snapshot reconciliation keyed by declared identity fields
Searchable HTML, JSON summary, and CSV findings for different review workflows
verification: Sample exports produce deterministic findings
Malformed/schema-error cases are explicitly rejected
Source and run instructions allow independent reproduction
reproduce: Run the reconciler against the provided snapshots
Introduce a duplicate, missing record, or contradictory field
Compare HTML/JSON/CSV outputs for consistent findings
project-asset-inventory.html.limitations: The tool cannot establish that source inventory data are correct; reconciliation quality depends on matching keys and upstream data ownership.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Inventory reconciliation detects drift without silently changing identifiers or treating one feed as the sole truth.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Two fictional CSV inventories with duplicate IDs, inconsistent case, missing serials and conflicting owners.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Verify deterministic normalization, unmatched sets, conflicting records and explicit ambiguity labels.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A duplicate identifier silently merges unrelated assets or a missing source becomes a fabricated asset.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Original fixtures, normalization rules, sorted delta, unresolved conflicts and CLI test results.

project-kubernetes-lab.html.title: Kubernetes Operations Lab
project-kubernetes-lab.html.evidence: Manifests, run instructions, probe-decision fixtures, and failure/recovery exercises
project-kubernetes-lab.html.problem: A pod can be running while a service is unusable. The lab separates startup, readiness, liveness, endpoint membership, rollout state, and application response so failure behavior can be reasoned about correctly.
constraints: Disposable/local cluster only
Health probes must model service semantics rather than process existence alone
Operational exercises must remain reversible
architecture: Exercises for replacement, scaling, rolling update, and rollback
verification: Source/manifest evidence is public
Probe-decision fixtures demonstrate expected state transitions
A complete cluster acceptance run remains a separate operational step
reproduce: Create the disposable cluster from the documented manifests
Induce a bounded dependency/probe failure
Observe pod events, endpoints, restarts, service response, and rollback behavior
project-kubernetes-lab.html.limitations: The portfolio release does not claim a live production cluster rollout or production SLO validation.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Operational readiness cannot be inferred from a running pod alone.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Disposable-cluster fixture with failing readiness probe, a new image and an intentionally unhealthy service dependency.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Record readiness vs liveness, rollout health, service routing, rollback and repeatable cleanup.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: Rollout reports success while the service fails declared acceptance requests or cleanup leaves resources.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Manifest hashes, kubectl observations, workload logs, requests and cluster-teardown record.

project-geometric-ai.html.title: Geometry & Physics Lab
project-geometric-ai.html.posture: Working numerical/research lab with upstream attribution
project-geometric-ai.html.evidence: Interactive lab, preserved GNP cases, methods documentation, executable notebooks, and pinned upstream research references
project-geometric-ai.html.problem: Research-inspired visualizations can overstate what has been measured. This project separates recorded predictions, live geometric calculations, analytic diffusion models, Bayesian inference, and external research provenance.
constraints: Historical saved predictions and live calculations must remain distinct
Upstream research code must be credited and license boundaries respected
Model-comparison claims require equal-information experiments and independent metrics
architecture: Bayesian/likelihood components plus reproducible notebook companions
verification: Six recorded GNP cases can be re-audited
Executable notebooks recompute selected metrics
Methods and pinned upstream references expose assumptions and provenance
reproduce: Run the working geometry lab
Recompute a saved benchmark or analytic diffusion case
Compare an equal-information baseline before drawing a model-superiority conclusion
project-geometric-ai.html.limitations: The lab does not claim that an interactive demo proves a general research result or that one model is universally superior.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Any reported geometric invariance or equivariance survives controlled coordinate transformations within numerical tolerance.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic point cloud with fixed seed; apply a known translation and rotation while holding features constant.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Compare invariant scalar outputs and equivariant vector outputs against transformed predictions; report error norms.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A claimed invariant changes materially under an admissible rigid transform without explanation.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Seed, point cloud, transformation matrix, model outputs, residuals, tolerance and attribution.

project-qpe.html.title: Quantum Phase Estimation
project-qpe.html.evidence: Interactive probability model, executable notebooks, inverse-DFT reference calculations, and explicit noise-model boundaries
project-qpe.html.problem: Phase estimation can look precise while error metrics are misleading near the 0/1 wrap boundary. The project exposes ideal distributions, finite-shot behavior, circular error, and an explicitly illustrative noise model.
constraints: Classical ideal-state simulation only
Circular phase distance must be distinguished from naive linear error
Noise illustrations must not be presented as calibrated hardware noise
architecture: Circular error metrics and bounded illustrative noise controls
verification: Exact-grid and off-grid phases provide known reference behaviors
Independent inverse-DFT notebook computes ideal probabilities
Wrap-boundary cases exercise circular error handling
reproduce: Run an exact binary phase
Run an off-grid and near-wrap phase
Compare ideal probabilities, sampled outcomes, and circular versus linear error
project-qpe.html.limitations: This does not implement a controlled hardware unitary or characterize a real quantum device.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Ideal quantum phase estimation yields phase-encoded measurement probabilities consistent with the model circuit.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Eigenphases 1/8, 3/8 and a non-dyadic fraction, using three counting qubits and multiple shot counts.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Compare analytic outcome probabilities, phase-estimate rounding and seeded finite-shot variation.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: An exact dyadic phase yields an incompatible peak, probabilities fail to normalize or shot noise is hidden.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Phase, qubit count, ideal distribution, sample frequencies, seed, error analysis and no-hardware disclaimer.

project-emergent.html.title: Emergent Systems Explorer
project-emergent.html.evidence: Seeded simulation, explicit numerical method, time-step refinement fixture, and ensemble extension path
project-emergent.html.problem: Collective-looking behavior can be an artifact of seed choice, integration step, or presentation. The project makes local coupling rules and numerical assumptions inspectable.
constraints: Seed and time step must be controlled during comparisons
Visualization cannot be treated as evidence of fundamental physics
Claims must separate model behavior from physical interpretation
architecture: Explicit Euler-style numerical evolution with coupling controls
verification: Fixed-fixture time-step refinement checks numerical sensitivity
Multiple seeds can be compared at fixed coupling
Browser behavior is deterministic for the same seed/settings
reproduce: Hold initial conditions fixed and change the time step
Repeat the same coupling value across multiple seeds
Compare synchronization metrics rather than relying only on the animation
project-emergent.html.limitations: This is a model of networked oscillators; it does not claim to reproduce the universe or a fundamental physical law.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Collective synchronization depends on coupling, initial conditions and finite-system effects.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Fixed-seed oscillator population with varied coupling and initial phase distribution; repeat across independent seeds.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Track order parameter, transient behavior and convergence sensitivity rather than asserting a universal threshold.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A single favorable seed is represented as proof of a general law or numerical step changes the claim without notice.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Differential equation, integration step, seed list, coupling sweep and uncertainty discussion.

project-mind.html.title: Project MIND Agent Workbench
project-mind.html.evidence: Inspectable planner, evidence ledger, verifier, dry-run executor, source design, and deterministic coordination fixtures
project-mind.html.problem: Agent systems can produce persuasive narratives without durable evidence. This project treats planning, artifacts, verification, acceptance criteria, and proposed actions as separate inspectable objects.
constraints: No claim of autonomous external execution
Every claimed outcome must point to an artifact or verifier result
Replay and stale-result handling matter before connecting live tools
architecture: Evidence ledger records typed artifacts and acceptance criteria
Verifier/dry-run layer separates proposed action from observed result
verification: Deterministic in-memory fixtures exercise coordination behavior
Replay can be compared against prior artifacts
No external LLM/tool execution is needed to inspect the workflow mechanics
reproduce: Open the working agent lab
Run a bounded planning/verifier scenario
Inspect the evidence ledger and distinguish planned, executed, and verified states
project-mind.html.limitations: The portfolio model does not run live distributed agents, external tools, or consensus protocols.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A bounded agent workflow can preserve artifacts, denied actions and replay behavior in an inspectable execution trace.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic task requiring research, synthesis and review; include a denied tool permission and repeated instruction.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Check explicit handoff ownership, artifact provenance, idempotency on retry and failure visibility.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A denied tool still runs, output cites nonexistent evidence or repeated execution duplicates side effects.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Task graph, agent/tool contract, permission log, artifacts and acceptance checks.

project-battle-chess.html.title: Crown & Ash
project-battle-chess.html.evidence: Playable browser build, public source, legal-move engine, game documentation, and validation notes

Launcher, game state, rendering, and AI/opponent behavior must not corrupt one another
Browser performance and input accessibility constrain visual complexity
architecture: Chess rules/state engine separated from 3D presentation
Five themed armies mapped onto legal piece behavior
Local two-player and computer-opponent paths with animated capture sequencing
verification: Dedicated playable build exercises end-to-end interaction
Source and validation notes are public
Game acceptance includes launch, move legality, capture animation, restart, and return flow
reproduce: Open the dedicated game build
Play legal and illegal move cases
Exercise local/computer play, captures, restart, and menu return
project-battle-chess.html.limitations: The project is a playable prototype under productization; portfolio evidence does not imply finished commercial QA or Steam release acceptance.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: The playable chess prototype should preserve legal chess outcomes as well as presentation and input behavior.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Known legal chess positions exercising castling, en passant, promotion, checkmate, draw and restart across keyboard/touch controls.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Compare move legality and terminal-state transitions to independent known positions without altering game code.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: An illegal move is accepted, a legal special move is rejected or restart retains stale state.

project-network-digital-twin.html.title: Network Digital Twin & Change Risk Engine
project-network-digital-twin.html.evidence: Deterministic synthetic topology, failure injection, change-risk scoring, and inspectable decision output
project-network-digital-twin.html.problem: Network changes are often reviewed as configuration text instead of system behavior. This lab models topology, redundancy, reachability, and intended resilience before a change reaches production.
constraints: Synthetic topology only
Risk decisions must expose the path and redundancy evidence behind them
A model must never be presented as a substitute for source-of-truth validation
architecture: Graph topology with redundant core/distribution/edge paths
Rollback trigger derived from loss of redundancy or reachability
verification: Baseline and injected failures produce deterministic expected outcomes
Single-path conditions are surfaced explicitly
All data are synthetic and browser-local
reproduce: Run the baseline topology
Inject a link failure or planned change
Compare reachability, resilience score, and rollback decision
project-network-digital-twin.html.limitations: This is a portfolio digital-twin model; it does not ingest or modify a production network.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Declared redundancy and path diversity can be tested under one specified failure at a time.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic core/distribution/edge topology with baseline alternate route; remove one uplink and change one policy.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Compute reachability and count independent paths before and after perturbation; disclose the scoring formula.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A risk score changes without a traceable rule, or a modeled single point of failure is missed.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Topology graph, constraints, fault injection, expected path set, scored output and limitations.

project-wireless-roaming-correlator.html.title: Wireless Roaming Evidence Correlator
project-wireless-roaming-correlator.html.evidence: Synthetic client event timeline, RF telemetry, roaming/authentication events, and ranked hypotheses
project-wireless-roaming-correlator.html.problem: Wireless incidents are misdiagnosed when RF conditions, client roaming, authentication, and retry data are reviewed in separate tools and time windows.
constraints: Synthetic telemetry only
Correlation must preserve contradictory evidence
Site-wide RF conclusions require site-wide evidence
architecture: Hypothesis ranking with supporting and contradicting signals
verification: Roaming/authentication case and stable-RF case produce different hypotheses
Localized retry spikes do not automatically become facility-wide interference claims
All windows are deterministic
reproduce: Analyze the roam/authentication window
Switch to the stable-RF trace
Compare how the hypothesis changes when the evidence changes
project-wireless-roaming-correlator.html.limitations: This lab does not query a live controller or spectrum analyzer; production diagnosis requires sanitized real telemetry and device context.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Time-aligned WLAN evidence can narrow hypotheses without mistaking temporal correlation for root cause.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Fabricated AP/client timeline containing a PMKID rejection, roaming attempt, RSSI trend and independently stable RF utilization.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Align clocks and distinguish client events, controller events and AP aggregate metrics; compute what each source proves.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: The model attributes an RF-wide root cause solely from one client event or collapses unrelated MAC addresses.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Synthetic timestamps, schema, clock-offset assumptions, correlation table and alternate explanations.

project-routing-convergence-lab.html.title: Routing Convergence & Failure Lab
project-routing-convergence-lab.html.evidence: Synthetic weighted topology, route-cost changes, link-failure injection, and deterministic path selection
project-routing-convergence-lab.html.problem: Redundancy is only useful if alternate paths are understood before failure. This lab makes path cost, failure domains, and convergence decisions visible.
constraints: Synthetic routed domain
No claim of protocol-complete BGP/OSPF behavior
Alternate-path reasoning must remain loop-free and deterministic
architecture: Path-selection engine based on modeled costs
verification: Baseline, metric-change, and preferred-link-failure scenarios have known expected paths
Loop-free alternate path remains visible
Output is deterministic for a given topology
reproduce: Observe the baseline selected path
Change a metric
Fail the preferred link and verify alternate selection
project-routing-convergence-lab.html.limitations: The current model abstracts protocol timers, route-policy complexity, ECMP, and real control-plane state.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A routing model selects valid least-cost paths and avoids loops after a controlled failure.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Weighted four-router directed graph with equal-cost and unequal-cost alternatives; fail the preferred edge.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Recompute routes and next hops independently; measure modeled updates and distinguish them from real convergence timers.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: An invalid path persists after link removal, route costs are inconsistent or a forwarding loop appears.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Topology, path-weight calculation, before/after forwarding table and explicitly simulated timing.

project-edge-5g-failover.html.title: Edge & 5G Failover Orchestrator
project-edge-5g-failover.html.evidence: Synthetic path telemetry, SLA-aware health scoring, failover decision, and hysteresis-oriented recovery reasoning
project-edge-5g-failover.html.problem: Interface-up state is not a sufficient failover signal for latency-sensitive edge systems. The lab evaluates loss, latency, and jitter against service objectives before moving traffic.
constraints: Synthetic WAN/5G data
Failover must avoid oscillation
Policy must distinguish service quality from carrier state
architecture: Primary/backup decision model with recovery hysteresis
verification: Healthy primary remains selected
Degraded primary moves traffic to 5G backup
Recovery case distinguishes immediate health from safe return
reproduce: Run baseline wired/5G telemetry
Degrade the wired path
Recover the primary and inspect the decision rationale
project-edge-5g-failover.html.limitations: This lab does not configure a modem/router or move real traffic; production integration requires device telemetry and change controls.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Failover decisions must be based on measured service objectives and explicit hysteresis, not merely link-up state.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic wired and cellular paths with changing latency, loss, jitter and a flapping threshold.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Calculate eligibility across consecutive samples; verify failover, failback and minimum hold-down rules.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: An isolated transient repeatedly flips active paths or selection ignores critical service thresholds.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Policy thresholds, time series, selected paths, transitions and cellular coverage limitations.

project-rust-flow-telemetry.html.title: Rust Flow Telemetry Engine
project-rust-flow-telemetry.html.posture: Source-backed Rust prototype plus working browser companion
project-rust-flow-telemetry.html.evidence: Rust source, Cargo manifest, synthetic CSV fixtures, browser aggregation model, and explicit non-capture boundary
project-rust-flow-telemetry.html.problem: Network telemetry pipelines need efficient aggregation without hiding the data model. The project groups synthetic flows into top talkers, protocol mix, packet/byte totals, and latency signals.
constraints: Synthetic flow records only
Standard-library implementation keeps dependencies minimal
No packet capture/eBPF claim until a Linux lab adapter exists
architecture: Rust CSV ingestion using standard library
Separate browser companion for inspectable presentation
verification: Synthetic CSV has known aggregation results
Rust source and Cargo manifest are publicly inspectable
Browser companion mirrors the aggregation concept
reproduce: Inspect the Rust source and sample CSV
Run the browser aggregation/filter cases
Compile/run the CLI in a Rust environment and compare its grouped output
project-rust-flow-telemetry.html.limitations: The current Rust component aggregates fixture data; it does not capture production traffic, attach eBPF, or export live telemetry.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: The flow analyzer aggregates records reproducibly without altering fixture fields or confusing bytes and packets.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Fixture containing TCP/UDP flows, duplicate records and malformed fields with declared time windows.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Independently sum packet/byte counters and compare groupings, sorting and invalid-record handling.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: The UI silently drops malformed data as valid or totals change with input record order without specification.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Fixture, CLI invocation, program output, expected aggregates and numerical checks.

project-incident-evidence-graph.html.title: Incident Correlation & Evidence Graph
project-incident-evidence-graph.html.evidence: Deterministic multi-domain event timeline, evidence weights, conflicting-signal case, and ranked hypotheses
project-incident-evidence-graph.html.problem: Incident response slows down when network, host, security, and application evidence are reduced to disconnected alerts. This lab correlates signals while preserving why a hypothesis was ranked.
constraints: Synthetic incident data
No opaque model may override evidence
Contradictory evidence must lower confidence instead of disappearing
architecture: Hypothesis ranking with explicit evidence ledger
verification: Baseline correlation and conflicting-evidence scenario produce different confidence
Evidence remains visible behind the ranking
All event sequences are deterministic
reproduce: Run the baseline incident
Inject a conflicting security signal
Compare the top hypothesis and confidence change
project-incident-evidence-graph.html.limitations: This is a deterministic evidence model, not a production AIOps platform or autonomous incident responder.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Correlated events should yield inspectable hypotheses rather than a single unjustified asserted cause.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic mixed logs with clock skew, coincident alerts, a false-positive event and an actual dependency failure.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Normalize time and identify corroborated causal chains; report evidence supporting and refuting each hypothesis.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A merely simultaneous alert is elevated to proven root cause or negative evidence is suppressed.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Clock mapping, event table, graph edges, ranked hypotheses, rejected explanations and review notes.

project-zero-trust-blast-radius.html.title: Zero Trust Policy & Blast-Radius Analyzer
project-zero-trust-blast-radius.html.evidence: Synthetic identity/device/resource graph, deterministic policy evaluation, drift scenario, and blast-radius output
project-zero-trust-blast-radius.html.problem: Access decisions become dangerous when identity, device posture, network zone, resource sensitivity, and policy exceptions are evaluated separately. This project models those contexts together so an evaluator can see both the authorization decision and the exposure created by policy drift.
constraints: Synthetic identities/resources only
Policy evaluation must be deterministic and explainable
Broad exceptions must expose their resulting blast radius
architecture: Context graph for identity, device, zone, and resource
Exposure map that highlights over-broad policy drift
verification: Baseline least-privilege request is allowed
Drift scenario expands risk and changes the decision
Reasoning inputs remain visible
reproduce: Evaluate the baseline request
Introduce the broad exception
Compare decision, risk, drift state, and blast radius
project-zero-trust-blast-radius.html.limitations: This does not connect to a real IAM, Conditional Access, or segmentation platform.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Least-privilege policy analysis should surface effective decisions and potential exposure paths from declared data.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic identities, device postures, zones and resource sensitivity; include a deny override and malformed policy.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Enumerate allow/deny matrix, compare policy precedence and quantify reachable protected nodes.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A denied principal gains reachability or a policy score is reported as enforcement by a real identity provider.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Policy fixture, decision trace, precedence model, blast-radius graph and explicit non-enforcement status.

project-distributed-chaos-recovery.html.title: Distributed Systems Chaos & Recovery Lab
project-distributed-chaos-recovery.html.evidence: Deterministic five-node quorum model, partition injection, leader failure, and invariant-oriented output
project-distributed-chaos-recovery.html.problem: Distributed systems should be designed around failure rather than tested only in healthy state. The lab shows how quorum and partitions affect availability and correctness.
constraints: Educational deterministic model
Quorum rules must remain explicit
Availability must not be confused with correctness
verification: Healthy, partitioned, and leader-loss cases produce expected quorum outcomes
Minority partition cannot commit writes
Leader loss remains survivable while quorum exists
reproduce: Run healthy state
Partition the cluster
Fail the leader and compare availability/invariant output
project-distributed-chaos-recovery.html.limitations: This is not a full consensus implementation; it abstracts election timers, log replication, and network timing.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: An abstract distributed service should expose partition and retry failure modes without claiming full consensus safety.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Three synthetic nodes and a partition, duplicate client request, delayed event and subsequent recovery.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Track state transitions and convergence after healing; verify the idempotency rule and bounded assumptions.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A contradictory pair of leaders is labeled safe without an acknowledged consensus model or replay duplicates an effect.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Initial state, injected fault timeline, transition trace, recovery criteria and unmodeled consensus details.

project-hpc-fabric-scheduler.html.title: GPU/HPC Fabric-Aware Scheduler
project-hpc-fabric-scheduler.html.evidence: Synthetic GPU inventory, memory constraints, fabric-locality scoring, hotspot scenario, and placement explanation
project-hpc-fabric-scheduler.html.problem: First-fit scheduling wastes accelerator systems when memory capacity, GPU count, communication topology, and fabric contention all influence job performance. This project makes those placement tradeoffs explicit instead of treating every available accelerator as equivalent.
constraints: Synthetic fabric only
Placement rationale must remain inspectable
Communication locality and memory constraints must be explicit
verification: Baseline single-node placement minimizes communication cost
Hotspot scenario changes the preferred placement
Scores and resource constraints are visible
reproduce: Schedule the baseline workload
Inject a fabric hotspot
Compare placement and score changes
project-hpc-fabric-scheduler.html.limitations: This is an educational scheduler model; it does not submit jobs to Slurm, Kubernetes, or a real GPU fabric.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Placement heuristics should account for compute fit and communication cost, not only theoretical accelerator utilization.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Small synthetic GPU cluster with heterogeneous memory, network links and two jobs with different communication demands.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Check allocation constraints and compare completion estimates against a simple independent schedule.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: An impossible placement passes memory constraints or predicted latency ignores the stated fabric penalty.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Cluster configuration, workload costs, allocation trace, bound/sensitivity calculation and no-real-cluster disclaimer.

project-hybrid-quantum-orchestrator.html.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Orchestrator
project-hybrid-quantum-orchestrator.html.evidence: Synthetic workload classes, CPU/GPU/QPU suitability scoring, queue-cost scenario, and explicit classical verification step
project-hybrid-quantum-orchestrator.html.problem: A hybrid system should use specialized compute only when the workload and operating conditions justify it. This lab models backend suitability instead of assuming QPU use is always desirable.
constraints: Educational model only
QPU suitability must be separated from queue/cost constraints
Classical verification remains part of the workflow
architecture: Decision trace with required verification path
verification: Baseline selects a QPU only for a candidate task
High QPU queue reroutes the task
Every decision exposes the reason
reproduce: Route the baseline workload set
Increase the QPU queue
Compare backend selection and verification requirements
project-hybrid-quantum-orchestrator.html.limitations: The lab does not submit circuits to a real QPU or claim quantum advantage.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Hybrid scheduling should make a quantum route conditional on an explicit estimated advantage and its overheads.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Two synthetic workloads with classical runtime, circuit depth, QPU queue delay, shot count and transfer cost.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Compute total wall-clock estimates, choose the lower-cost feasible plan and show how queue delay changes the decision.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A purported quantum advantage ignores queue, error and sampling overhead or implies hardware execution.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Cost model, assumptions, decision log, sensitivity study and no-QPU-use statement.

project-event-sourced-workflow-engine.ht.title: Event-Sourced Workflow Engine
project-event-sourced-workflow-engine.ht.evidence: Deterministic state machine, immutable event sequence, duplicate-delivery scenario, and replay behavior
project-event-sourced-workflow-engine.ht.problem: Long-running workflows become fragile when current state is mutated without a durable record of how it changed. This lab makes state transitions replayable and retry-safe.
constraints: Deterministic synthetic workflow
Retries must not duplicate side effects
Event history must reconstruct state
verification: Worker-failure case redelivers an event without duplicating the effect
Replay reconstructs the expected aggregate state
State changes remain auditable
reproduce: Run the baseline workflow
Inject worker failure and observe deduplication
Replay the event stream and compare the reconstructed state
project-event-sourced-workflow-engine.ht.limitations: The lab models event sourcing in-browser; it does not include durable distributed storage, a message broker, or production saga execution.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Event replay and idempotency preserve deterministic state reconstruction under duplicate and out-of-order inputs.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic account/workflow event log with duplicate event IDs and a later schema-version change.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Replay to expected state, reject duplicates according to policy and compare state after serialization reload.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: Two replays of the same accepted event stream produce different states or an invalid event mutates state.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Event schema, ordered log, snapshots, expected state and schema-evolution assumptions.

project-api-contract-compatibility.html.title: API Contract Compatibility Analyzer
project-api-contract-compatibility.html.evidence: Synthetic contract diffs, breaking/additive scenarios, compatibility classification, and release-gate output
project-api-contract-compatibility.html.problem: APIs fail consumers when seemingly small schema changes are released without compatibility analysis. The lab treats the API contract as a versioned engineering artifact.
constraints: Synthetic contracts
Compatibility rules must be explicit
Release decision must distinguish additive from breaking changes
architecture: Policy gate that blocks incompatible releases
verification: Removed response fields and new required inputs are classified as breaking
Optional/additive fields remain compatible
Release decision changes deterministically with the diff
reproduce: Run baseline contract comparison
Introduce breaking changes
Add compatible optional fields and compare the release gate
project-api-contract-compatibility.html.limitations: This model does not yet import a complete OpenAPI specification or consumer-specific contract suite.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: API changes should be evaluated from consumer-visible contract semantics, not only textual diffs.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Version A/B synthetic API contracts where one optional response field becomes required and one type changes.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Classify changes by request/response compatibility, identify affected consumers and document conditional cases.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A breaking input requirement is labeled universally backward-compatible without consumer assumptions.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Old/new fixture contracts, rule rationale, category and counterexample consumer.

project-database-migration-safety.html.title: Database Migration Safety Planner
project-database-migration-safety.html.evidence: Destructive migration scenario, expand/contract plan, risk classification, and rollback analysis
project-database-migration-safety.html.problem: Schema changes can be syntactically valid and still create locks, version incompatibility, data loss, or impossible rollbacks. This project evaluates database evolution as a coordinated software-release problem in which old and new application versions may need to coexist safely.
constraints: Synthetic migration plans
Old and new application versions may coexist during rollout
Destructive operations require explicit retirement gates
verification: Direct destructive change is classified high risk
Expand/contract retains compatibility and a stronger rollback path
Risk rationale is visible per step
reproduce: Evaluate the baseline migration
Plan a destructive schema change
Convert it to expand/contract and compare risk/rollback output
project-database-migration-safety.html.limitations: The model abstracts database-engine-specific lock semantics and does not execute a live migration.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A staged migration can preserve compatibility and rollback while data is incrementally transformed.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Fictional database schema adding a required field using nullable-add, backfill, dual-read and final constraint.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Verify expand/migrate/contract sequence, batch resume behavior and pre/post query semantics.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: A rollback leaves inaccessible data or a newly required column breaks old clients during expansion.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Schema before/after, migration plan, query fixtures, failure injection and engine-specific caveats.

project-concurrent-job-scheduler.html.title: Concurrent Job Scheduler & Backpressure Lab
project-concurrent-job-scheduler.html.evidence: Bounded worker-pool model, priority queues, overload scenario, backpressure, and scaling behavior
project-concurrent-job-scheduler.html.problem: Concurrency systems collapse when work admission is unbounded. The lab models how capacity, priority, queue depth, and backpressure interact during overload.
constraints: Bounded concurrency
High-priority work must remain protected under load
Queue growth must become an explicit signal
architecture: Admission/backpressure policy driven by queue pressure
verification: Load spike increases queue depth and activates backpressure
High-priority SLA remains protected
Scaling workers changes throughput without removing queue ordering
reproduce: Run baseline workload
Spike the queue
Increase worker capacity and compare queue/admission behavior
project-concurrent-job-scheduler.html.limitations: The browser lab abstracts real threads, async runtimes, deadlines, and scheduler overhead.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A bounded scheduler should honor concurrency limits and apply backpressure under overload.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic arrivals with service times, queue capacity, worker count and one stalled job.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Measure queue depth, rejected/queued work, service time and fairness under increasing arrival rate.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: The queue grows without a bound under declared capacity or a rejected job is counted as completed.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Input timeline, scheduling policy, per-job trace, throughput/latency distribution and model limits.

project-cache-consistency-lab.html.title: Cache Consistency & Stampede Lab
project-cache-consistency-lab.html.evidence: Cache-aside baseline, hot-key invalidation scenario, single-flight mitigation, and origin-load metrics
project-cache-consistency-lab.html.problem: Caching can move failure from latency to consistency or overload. The lab exposes stale-read, invalidation, and thundering-herd tradeoffs.
constraints: Synthetic cache/origin model
Freshness policy must be explicit
Concurrent misses should not overwhelm the origin
architecture: Single-flight request coalescing for hot misses
verification: Hot-key invalidation increases origin load without coalescing
Single-flight collapses concurrent misses
Freshness and hit ratio remain visible
reproduce: Run baseline cache state
Invalidate the hot key
Enable single-flight and compare origin requests
project-cache-consistency-lab.html.limitations: The lab does not model a real distributed cache, network partitions, or multi-region consistency protocol.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A cache strategy should make stale data, expiry and stampede behavior explicit under concurrent misses.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic hot key with ten simultaneous requests, TTL expiry and an upstream read delay.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Compare unprotected origin load against a singleflight or stale-while-revalidate policy; record freshness constraints.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: The cache claims strong consistency while serving stale values or origin load is hidden in metrics.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Request trace, TTL policy, upstream calls, stale windows and consistency boundary.

project-progressive-delivery-control-pla.title: Progressive Delivery Control Plane
project-progressive-delivery-control-pla.evidence: Canary cohorts, SLO threshold, degradation scenario, staged promotion, and automated rollback decision
project-progressive-delivery-control-pla.problem: A deployment should be judged by runtime evidence before its blast radius expands. The lab models canary progression as a controlled decision process.
constraints: Synthetic release telemetry
SLO guardrails must control promotion
Rollback must be automatic when the canary violates policy
verification: Healthy canary is held/advanced within policy
Degraded canary exceeds the SLO and triggers rollback
Decision is tied to visible metrics
reproduce: Run baseline canary
Degrade the canary
Advance a healthy rollout and compare traffic/error metrics
project-progressive-delivery-control-pla.limitations: This does not deploy real workloads or integrate with a production GitOps/mesh platform.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A canary decision should combine traffic weights with SLO evidence and a bounded rollback policy.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Synthetic 1%/10%/50% exposure stages with latency/error distributions, small samples and an adverse regression.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Check sample adequacy, error-budget impact, promotion/abort thresholds and time-stamped decisions.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: An insufficient sample is presented as conclusive or the rollout promotes despite an explicit abort trigger.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Stage definitions, metric windows, confidence limitations, decision trace and rollback verification.

project-mini-compiler-static-analyzer.ht.title: Mini Compiler & Static Analyzer
project-mini-compiler-static-analyzer.ht.evidence: Tokenizer, parser/type-checker model, valid program, type-error scenario, and source-oriented diagnostics
project-mini-compiler-static-analyzer.ht.problem: Compiler construction forces software semantics to be explicit. The lab demonstrates how tokens, syntax trees, types, and diagnostics compose into a correctness pipeline.
constraints: Small educational language
Errors should be found before execution when statically decidable
Diagnostics must identify the source construct involved
verification: Valid numeric program produces zero type errors
STRING + NUMBER is rejected
Token/source locations remain visible
reproduce: Compile the valid sample
Introduce the type error
Inspect tokens and the resulting type-check failure
project-mini-compiler-static-analyzer.ht.limitations: The current lab is a compact compiler model; it does not yet generate bytecode/native code or implement full scopes/control flow.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: A miniature compiler should reject invalid syntax and preserve AST semantics through each demonstrated stage.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Small expression language with operators, precedence, variables, invalid tokens and undeclared names.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Compare token stream, parse tree, diagnostics and evaluated meaning against hand-calculated examples.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: An ambiguous parse silently changes precedence or an invalid symbol yields a valid result.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Grammar subset, input fixtures, expected AST, diagnostics, and explicit absence of production code generation.

project-reliable-message-processing.html.title: Reliable Message Processing & Transactional Outbox Lab
project-reliable-message-processing.html.evidence: At-least-once delivery model, duplicate-delivery scenario, idempotent-consumer mitigation, and outbox state
project-reliable-message-processing.html.problem: Distributed message delivery is often at-least-once, so consumers must be designed for duplicate delivery and database/publish failure boundaries.
constraints: At-least-once delivery semantics
Duplicate effects must be suppressed explicitly
Database state and message publication must not rely on an unsafe dual write
verification: Duplicate delivery exposes duplicate-side-effect risk
Idempotency suppresses repeated effects
Outbox state keeps persistence/publication boundary visible
reproduce: Run baseline message processing
Redeliver a message
Enable idempotency/outbox protection and compare outcomes
project-reliable-message-processing.html.limitations: The lab does not connect to a real broker or database and does not claim exactly-once transport semantics.

reviewProtocol.hypothesis: Transactional outbox design can prevent lost application intents while still permitting duplicate message delivery.
reviewProtocol.fixture: Fictional order transaction, outbox row, broker retry and crash between publish and acknowledgement.
reviewProtocol.oracle: Check persisted intent after commit, replay handling, consumer deduplication and eventual state invariants.
reviewProtocol.falsifier: The demonstration equates at-least-once broker delivery with transport exactly-once, or crash loses the committed intent.
reviewProtocol.evidence: Order/outbox tables, failure timeline, delivery log, deduplication key and boundary of the simulation.
